propositions: Six proposed deterministic clarity criteria were tested against a corpus of 574 closed, signed, and accepted historical tickets; each criterion failed to reject at least one valid completed ticket, disproving its unconditional applicability.

Required literal section headings (Approach, Scope) are overfitted; valid plans distribute semantic content across non-standard aliases and compact executable checklists (tickets 003d, 03c6), so heading presence must be narrowed or replaced by content-level normalization.

Per-AC explicit proof markers (verified by/verify with) are not necessary; tickets with precise behavioral oracles but no proof-sentinel passed both plan-review and completion-verifier (ticket 003d), making marker presence an advisory signal rather than a validity gate.

Edit-set and file_impact requirements are invalid for read-only analysis and operational work when an explicit no-edit/output contract is documented; ticket 0730 is a valid analysis probe with empty file_impact and durable comment-based output.

AC conjunction and complexity heuristics cannot reliably distinguish bundled independent deliverables from atomic cross-surface invariants; ticket 090f demonstrates coherent multi-conjunction matrices that splitting would obscure, making conjunction counts unsuitable as hard validity oracles.

Testing section presence should not trigger negative-scenario requirements on purely mechanical, non-user-facing work; ticket 35bc contains valid regression and invariant tests but lacks failure/edge/boundary markers because its scope (heading/weight migration) is inapplicable to user-flow taxonomy.
